units.rhetorical_move: opens on stability of the society
units.function: state the purpose before the tasks

original_instantiations: the system exists to keep society stable
a privacy pricing system is what gets established

units.source_excerpt: For ensuring the stability of the society, we establish a pricing system.
units.reusable_pattern: Open by naming the stability the system is meant to protect.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the purpose.

units.rhetorical_move: numbers the work as tasks
units.function: label each job with a task number

original_instantiations: each paragraph opens with a task number
the task then names its method

units.source_excerpt: Task one, we choose a stated number of indexes and divide them into categories.
units.reusable_pattern: Number each piece of work and name the method it uses.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge two tasks into one paragraph.

units.rhetorical_move: verifies with a simulation of people
units.function: close a task on a check

original_instantiations: a simulation of a stated number of people is run
it is used to verify feasibility

units.source_excerpt: A simulation of a stated number of people's information verifies the model's feasibility.
units.reusable_pattern: End a method paragraph by saying what the simulation verified.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the simulation proves the model.

units.rhetorical_move: calls the impact long tail
units.function: name an effect in two words

original_instantiations: the impact of leakage is called long tail
an actuarial model then computes the compensation

units.source_excerpt: The impact of data leakage is long tail, and an actuarial model computes the compensation.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the shape of an impact, then the model that prices it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not explain the effect at length.

units.rhetorical_move: closes on a sensitivity test
units.function: end the summary with the check

original_instantiations: a sensitivity test is performed last
its job is to verify stability

units.source_excerpt: Finally, we perform a sensitivity test to verify the stability of the model.
units.reusable_pattern: Close a summary with finally plus the test that checks stability.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add another task after it.

units.rhetorical_move: says commercialization becomes an important issue
units.function: move from a trend to a need

original_instantiations: commercialization of privacy is called an important issue
therefore a pricing system is needed

units.source_excerpt: With the development of informatization, commercialization becomes an important issue.
units.reusable_pattern: Derive the need for a system from a named development.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip the therefore.

units.rhetorical_move: restates the tasks as a list
units.function: turn the brief into numbered tasks

original_instantiations: the tasks follow as a numbered list
each one begins with consider

units.source_excerpt: Our tasks are as follows, each one beginning with what to consider.
units.reusable_pattern: Restate the brief as a numbered list of considerations.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not answer the tasks here.

units.rhetorical_move: draws the conclusion with thus it can be seen
units.function: summarize the citations first

original_instantiations: three cited studies are summed up
the summary says most people will sell for compensation

units.source_excerpt: Thus, it can be seen that most people are willing to sell privacy for compensation.
units.reusable_pattern: Sum up several citations with thus, it can be seen that.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not attribute the conclusion to one source.

units.rhetorical_move: says the pricing system should be set up
units.function: move from willingness to a requirement

original_instantiations: willingness to sell is established
so a suitable pricing system ought to be created

units.source_excerpt: So the appropriate pricing system should be set up.
units.reusable_pattern: Turn a finding into a requirement with so and should.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave the finding without the requirement.

units.rhetorical_move: compares information to a spider web
units.function: justify a category with an image

original_instantiations: social contact is generated through life
it is compared to spider web information

units.source_excerpt: Social contact is generated in the process of life with the other spider web information.
units.reusable_pattern: Justify one category with a concrete image.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not explain the image away.

units.rhetorical_move: splits parameters into difficult and quantifiable
units.function: divide before choosing methods

original_instantiations: five parameters split into two categories
one is hard to quantify and the other is not

units.source_excerpt: We divide the parameters into those difficult to quantify and those we can quantify.
units.reusable_pattern: Split the inputs by whether they can be quantified.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not apply one method to both groups.

units.rhetorical_move: says we empower each parameter
units.function: keep empower for weighting

original_instantiations: each parameter is empowered
the method used is a hierarchy process

units.source_excerpt: We empower each parameter by a hierarchy process.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep empower where the writer means assign a weight.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not replace empower with weight when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: says privacy seems difficult but can be quantified
units.function: concede the difficulty, then override it

original_instantiations: privacy information seems difficult to quantify
an appropriate method quantifies it to a certain extent

units.source_excerpt: Privacy seems difficult to quantify, but an appropriate method quantifies it to a certain extent.
units.reusable_pattern: Concede the difficulty with seems, then override it with but.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the concession.

units.rhetorical_move: calls one algorithm the most significant
units.function: praise a method absolutely

original_instantiations: one tree algorithm is described
it is called the most significant in machine learning at present

units.source_excerpt: This is the most significant algorithm in machine learning at present.
units.reusable_pattern: Praise a chosen method with the most significant at present.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften the superlative.

units.rhetorical_move: calls the deviation rate more ideal
units.function: prefer one measure for comparison

original_instantiations: a plain deviation is set aside
a rate is called more ideal for comparison

units.source_excerpt: It is more ideal to use a deviation rate so the parameters can be compared.
units.reusable_pattern: Prefer one measure by calling it more ideal.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the preferred measure is exact.

units.rhetorical_move: says bigger sensitivity means bigger value
units.function: chain two comparatives

original_instantiations: more sensitive information yields more rules
so the value of the information is bigger

units.source_excerpt: The more sensitive the information, the bigger its value.
units.reusable_pattern: Link sensitivity to value with two comparatives.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not break the chain into separate claims.

units.rhetorical_move: reports the price floats in a range
units.function: give a band, not a point

original_instantiations: privacy cost is computed per person
it floats between two stated amounts

units.source_excerpt: The privacy cost floats between two stated amounts.
units.reusable_pattern: Report a result as floating between two bounds.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not collapse the band to its midpoint.

units.rhetorical_move: prices the person who provides everything
units.function: give the extreme case

original_instantiations: providing every item of privacy is the extreme
it returns one stated yearly total

units.source_excerpt: If a person provides all privacy information, the yearly total reaches one stated sum.
units.reusable_pattern: State the all-provided case and its total separately from the band.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the extreme as the typical price.

units.rhetorical_move: caps the profit margin
units.function: borrow a market range

original_instantiations: ordinary goods earn a stated margin band
the privacy seller may not exceed its top

units.source_excerpt: The profit margin of a commodity is a stated band, and the seller cannot exceed its top.
units.reusable_pattern: Cap a margin by borrowing the range for ordinary goods.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not apply the luxury margin.

units.rhetorical_move: splits the market into three periods
units.function: stage the life cycle

original_instantiations: the market passes through development, maturity and decline
each stage has its own elasticity

units.source_excerpt: We divide the market into a development period, a mature period and a decline period.
units.reusable_pattern: Stage a market into three named periods.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a fourth period.

units.rhetorical_move: predicts a price-free phenomenon
units.function: name the end state

original_instantiations: years of selling drive the market to saturation
a price-free phenomenon may then appear

units.source_excerpt: Once the market nears saturation, there may be a price-free phenomenon.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the end state as a phenomenon that may appear.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assert the phenomenon as certain.

units.rhetorical_move: assumes same conditions mean same willingness
units.function: state the assumption, then the reality it ignores

original_instantiations: people in the same conditions share one willingness
in reality each person differs and the spread is roughly normal

units.source_excerpt: People with the same conditions are assumed to share one willingness, though in reality they differ.
units.reusable_pattern: State an assumption and concede the reality it sets aside.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use the assumption outside its conditions.

units.rhetorical_move: excludes special fields
units.function: name what the model leaves out

original_instantiations: political and military fields are excluded
their consequences cannot be quantified by general standards

units.source_excerpt: We do not consider personal information from special fields such as politics and the military.
units.reusable_pattern: Exclude a class of cases and say why it cannot be quantified.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not apply the prices to the excluded fields.

units.rhetorical_move: says privacy should not be fully protected as a right
units.function: take a position and split the object

original_instantiations: full protection as a human right is rejected
information is split into personality and property elements

units.source_excerpt: Information privacy should not be protected fully as a human right.
units.reusable_pattern: Reject full protection, then split the thing into two elements.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not restore the full protection later.

units.rhetorical_move: says expectations get higher and higher
units.function: stack the comparative

original_instantiations: familiarity with disclosure grows over time
expectations of return get higher and higher

units.source_excerpt: People's expectations for the return of privacy are getting higher and higher.
units.reusable_pattern: Intensify a trend by repeating the comparative.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not cap the trend with a number.

units.rhetorical_move: reports the fitting degree and praises it
units.function: give the statistic, then the judgment

original_instantiations: one fit returns a stated measure of fit
the fitting effect is then called very good

units.source_excerpt: We get a high fitting degree, so the fitting effect is very good.
units.reusable_pattern: Follow a fit statistic with the fitting effect is very good.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the judgment.

units.rhetorical_move: offers two levels of calculation
units.function: give the reader a choice of precision

original_instantiations: a careful calculation raises each dimension
an overall calculation may use the average growth instead

units.source_excerpt: For an overall calculation, the average growth value can be used.
units.reusable_pattern: Offer a precise option and a coarser one.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the average as the only choice.

units.rhetorical_move: finds non-sellers get implicated
units.function: report the spillover

original_instantiations: a network model of leakage is built
people who never sell are increasingly implicated

units.source_excerpt: Individuals who do not sell privacy are increasingly implicated as the market develops.
units.reusable_pattern: Report that non-participants are implicated by others' sales.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not limit the harm to the sellers.

units.rhetorical_move: says the dilemma needs a limit on selling
units.function: move from a bad equilibrium to a rule

original_instantiations: without intervention the group reaches a bad equilibrium
limiting personal selling is called necessary

units.source_excerpt: To escape the dilemma, limiting the sale of personal privacy is necessary.
units.reusable_pattern: Call a restriction necessary once an equilibrium is shown to be bad.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the restriction as optional.

units.rhetorical_move: says leakage brings an economic crisis
units.function: chain the decline to a crisis

original_instantiations: leakage lowers the value and the willingness to sell
the trading market then faces an economic crisis

units.source_excerpt: The decline in value and willingness will lead to an economic crisis of the trading market.
units.reusable_pattern: Carry a decline through to a named crisis.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not stop at the decline.

units.rhetorical_move: says the impact rises, drops, then fluctuates
units.function: give the shape over time

original_instantiations: one effect can be restrained by the other
the impact rises first, then drops, with fluctuations

units.source_excerpt: The impact will rise first, then drop, and there will be fluctuations in it.
units.reusable_pattern: Describe an impact by its order: rise, drop, fluctuate.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not smooth the fluctuations out.

units.rhetorical_move: keeps both readings of one test
units.function: leave the contradiction

original_instantiations: one probability is said to accept the original hypothesis
a larger one is said to reject it

units.source_excerpt: One reported probability accepts the hypothesis and the next rejects it.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep both readings where the text contradicts itself.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reconcile the two readings.

units.rhetorical_move: concludes the stability is good
units.function: close the test on a plain judgment

original_instantiations: the two sets of prices show no significant difference
therefore the stability of the model is sound

units.source_excerpt: There is no significant difference, so the stability of the model is good.
units.reusable_pattern: Close a test with so the stability is good.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not upgrade good to proven.

units.rhetorical_move: says the model reflects all aspects
units.function: claim completeness

original_instantiations: many basic and derived parameters are considered
the model is said to reflect the impact of all aspects

units.source_excerpt: The model reflects the impact of all aspects.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim coverage with all aspects.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not list the aspects the model skips.

units.rhetorical_move: calls the model simple but flexible and reliable
units.function: stack three qualities

original_instantiations: the model is simple
it is also flexible and reliable, adjusted by a simple adjustment

units.source_excerpt: The model is simple but flexible and reliable.
units.reusable_pattern: Praise a model with three qualities joined by but.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a fourth.

units.rhetorical_move: says not all people can accept it
units.function: state the limit with a doubled modal

original_instantiations: consent is denied for the whole population
one modal sits directly atop a second

units.source_excerpt: It is impossible for all people can accept the commercialization of privacy.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the stacked modal as the writer's phrasing.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not repair the grammar when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: says the areas are not exhaustive
units.function: admit incomplete coverage

original_instantiations: certain inputs must be retuned to circumstances
the ground covered stops short of everything

units.source_excerpt: The areas involved are not exhaustive.
units.reusable_pattern: Admit the coverage is not exhaustive in one short sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name the missing areas.

units.rhetorical_move: addresses a dear decision maker
units.function: open the letter on the reader

original_instantiations: the letter opens with a salutation
it then says information grows more and more important

units.source_excerpt: Dear decision maker: information becomes more and more important.
units.reusable_pattern: Open a policy letter by addressing the reader directly.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open on a result.

units.rhetorical_move: says a gap results in huge risks
units.function: blame the risk on a missing law

original_instantiations: laws and pricing strategies still have a large gap
the gap results in huge risks

units.source_excerpt: The policies still exist in a large gap, resulting in huge risks.
units.reusable_pattern: Trace a risk back to a gap in policy.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not blame the sellers.

units.rhetorical_move: says a system of privacy is worth more
units.function: contrast the bundle with the piece

original_instantiations: a single piece of privacy has its price
the same piece inside a system is worth more

units.source_excerpt: Other things being equal, privacy inside a system is worth more than a single piece.
units.reusable_pattern: Contrast a bundled value with a single one, holding other things equal.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the hedge.

units.rhetorical_move: says the float is small enough
units.function: judge the model by a bound

original_instantiations: the same crowd differs only a little
the overall float stays under a stated amount

units.source_excerpt: The overall float stays under a stated amount, so the model meets expectations.
units.reusable_pattern: Accept a model once its float stays under a stated bound.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not ignore the bound.

units.rhetorical_move: sells only if use is reasonable
units.function: attach a condition to willingness

original_instantiations: more than half would sell at the stated price
only if the information is used reasonably and threatens nobody

units.source_excerpt: Most people will sell at this price, but only if the information is used reasonably.
units.reusable_pattern: Attach willingness to a condition with but only if.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the condition.

units.rhetorical_move: says the government must want to regulate
units.function: keep the doubled modal

original_instantiations: unexpected market conditions must be avoided
the government must want to regulate

units.source_excerpt: The government must want to undertake certain regulation and limit the price.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep must want as the writer's phrasing.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reduce it to must when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: says deal with it as soon as possible
units.function: close the list on urgency

original_instantiations: four responses to a leak are listed
the last says to handle it as soon as possible

units.source_excerpt: Deal with the unexpected situation as soon as possible.
units.reusable_pattern: End a response list with as soon as possible.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a fifth response.

units.rhetorical_move: numbers sources in brackets
units.function: keep the citation format

original_instantiations: each source opens with a bracketed number
two entries repeat the same citation

units.source_excerpt: Sources open with a bracketed number, and two entries repeat one citation.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the bracketed numbering, repeats included.
prohibited_generalizations: The citation list belongs to this paper and does not transfer.

units.rhetorical_move: prints the code that produced the coefficients
units.function: point at the program

original_instantiations: the gradient boosting program is printed in full
its printed importances match the coefficients used

units.source_excerpt: The appendix prints the program that produced the coefficients.
units.reusable_pattern: Point the reader to the printed program instead of repeating it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reproduce the program in the body.
